author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Singer and television host Jennifer Hudson visited the Charlestown Boys & Girls Club during a recent Boston stop, meeting members and offering encouragement to young people interested in performing.

Hudson answered questions from students and spoke about continuing to pursue a goal even when fear is present. The visit had a personal connection: she took part in a Boys & Girls Club program while growing up in Chicago and told the Charlestown group that the experience helped shape her own path.

Club members also created a version of the “Spirit Tunnel,” the welcoming routine associated with Hudson’s daytime show. The appearance gave aspiring musicians and performers a chance to hear directly from an artist whose career has included music, film, theater and television.

Hudson was in the area promoting the fifth season of “The Jennifer Hudson Show,” which is scheduled to premiere Monday and air locally on WHDH. For the club, the visit paired a celebrity appearance with a practical message about persistence, confidence and making use of community programs that give young people room to develop their interests.
dek: The singer and talk-show host met Boys & Girls Club members, answered questions and shared advice with young people interested in music.
headline: Jennifer Hudson encourages young performers at Charlestown club
